parts.text: You just start your day without a plan.
How do you eat an elephant?
Your biggest task works the same way: break it into small steps, and start with the first one.
Brian Tracy says ten minutes of planning can save you up to two hours a day.
But here is the part most people miss:
make your list the night before.
According to Tracy, your mind keeps working on it while you sleep.
You wake up, and you already know what to do.
Use three lists: one for the month, one for the week, and one for the day.
Then tick off every task you finish.
Every check mark is proof that you are moving.
Alan Lakein said it best: planning is bringing the future into the present, so you can do something about it now.
Tonight, take ten minutes. Write tomorrow's list.
